title: Chunking: size, overlap and semantic boundaries

videos.script: A policy of nine hundred words, and an embedding model that reads two hundred and nineteen of them. {{limit}} Add a sentence at the end of the policy, and its vector does not move at all. {{same}} So documents are cut into chunks. The question is where. {{where}} Cut every sixty words, and every cut lands in the middle of a sentence. {{fixed}} Let the chunks overlap, and each sentence has a second chance to arrive whole. {{overlap}} Or cut where the author did, at the headings and between paragraphs. {{structure}} Or measure where the meaning changes, and cut there. {{semantic}} Each has an argument. Arguments do not settle it, so this lesson measures all of them on the same twenty-six questions. {{table}} How many answers each one finds, and what it costs in the prompt. {{trade}} On documents with good headings, the author's own marks win. {{end}}
